coverage.assessment: The maxim 'double standards are fatal to politicians' now floats free of Roosevelt and Lodge. The Senate's chronic intrigue no longer sets up Hay's six-vote feat. Seneca, the moth and Coal versus Gun remain causally intact.
In para 2, 'him'/'he' after 'Clarence King was...' could be read as King. 'These two minds' in para 17 lacks a clear antecedent. 'To them at sixty-three' and McKinley's death are clear.
Hay's quoted lament survives intact, but the cut of the condolence-letter frame loosens attribution to Hay. The refrain is correctly reused in Adams's voice in para 4.

The final paragraph drops the concession that Adams had at least mechanical certainty about Coal-powers and Gun-powers. His ignorance becomes unqualified. Other facts (ages, six votes, the order of England, France, Germany and Russia) are accurate.

There is no anticipation of Hay's death or the Russo-Japanese war. The third-person mocked 'student'/'moth' self-portrait persists. 'A student nurtured in ideas of the eighteenth century' was usefully restored.
The periodic, epigrammatic texture largely survives. Some ironic grace notes are cut: the 'rest-cure' irony, the moth's singed wings, and Lodge's 'now worshipping, now banning'.

The Adams/Lodge Bostonian mirror survives. The Lodge portrait loses its thesis that Lodge was the more interesting educational type, which the crows/plumage image resolves. The knowledge-to-ignorance reversal is slightly flattened.
All three dependencies are present at both endpoints in the published revisions of 009, 022 and 029. The Gun-power/inertia echo is weakened in the closing paragraph but survives in para 15.

dependencies.assessment: Seneca's lesson is framed as confirming the maxim ("His friends in power were lost"). The 009 revision retains the original rule.

evidence.quote: Seneca closed the vast circle of his knowledge by learning that a friend in power was a friend lost--a fact very much worth insisting upon.
the rule that a friend in power is a friend lost.

dependencies.assessment: Hay's lament keeps both King's promise and his lonely death. The 022 revision keeps 'One Clarence King' and the 'die at eighty the richest' forecast that the lament ironizes.

evidence.quote: the best and brightest man of his generation, with talents immeasurably beyond any of his contemporaries
With ordinary luck he would die at eighty the richest and most many-sided genius of his day.

dependencies.assessment: The Coal-power and Gun-power terms survive in para 15, and the Gun-power alternative merges Germany in Russia. The 029 revision keeps the empire of Coal and Russian inertia. The closing inertia echo was cut (see F4).

evidence.quote: persuading the Kaiser to join what might be called the Coal-power combination. The only possible alternative was a Gun-power combination formed by merging Germany in Russia.
one great empire was ruled by one great emperor--Coal.

findings.claim: The revision drops King's letter to Hay and the 'graveyard'/'funeral habit' frame. The sentence immediately before 'impressed him intensely... he said' now has Clarence King as its subject. Hay is last named at the paragraph's start.
findings.counterevidence: The lament's content describes King in the third person, so King cannot be the speaker. The paragraph opens with Hay's viewpoint.

Among the letters of condolence was one from Clarence King at Pasadena, "heart-breaking in grace and tenderness--the old King manner."
Clarence King was "simply waiting till nature and the foe have done their struggle." The tragedy of King impressed him intensely.

findings.minimal_repair: Change to 'impressed Hay intensely', or restore the clause 'Among the letters of condolence was one from Clarence King at Pasadena'.
findings.plan_relation: Required by the continuity check (Hay's attribution). The 'funeral habit' cut is optional.
findings.reader_effect: The plan requires the King quotation to be attributed to Hay first. The pronoun now invites a momentary misreading, and King's 'old King manner' grace no longer contrasts with his lonely death.
findings.title: King lament's speaker loosened by cutting the condolence-letter frame

findings.claim: The first draft cut 'Lodge had the singular merit of interesting'. The revision also removes 'As a type for study, Lodge was more interesting than the President' and 'now worshipping, now banning'. The crows/plumage contrast now follows the Shakespeare clause with no stated point.
findings.counterevidence: The Roosevelt/Lodge born-versus-taught contrast (V4) and the varied plumage still imply a favorable distinction.

findings.claim: The revision deletes the sentence in which Roosevelt and Lodge are liable to the shifting sands of opinion. 'Fatal to politicians' now jumps straight to 'In domestic politics the larger study...'.
findings.counterevidence: 'He was not a Senator' in para 10 still implies the contrast.

Double standards are inspiration to men of letters, but they are apt to be fatal to politicians. In domestic politics the larger study was lost in the ambitions of fifth-rate men.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's sentence after the maxim.
findings.plan_relation: Required: the essential item 'Double standards are fatal to politicians' and the plan's risk note on the mirrored Adams/Lodge Bostonian comparison.
findings.reader_effect: This loses the argumentative link that completes the Adams-versus-Senator mirror ('but he was not a Senator'). The transition to forces in politics is abrupt.

findings.claim: The revision cuts the sentence granting that Adams had at least the mechanical assurance of Coal-power intensities and Gun-power inertia. 'He conceived that had the Czar...' therefore no longer works as a counterpoint to that concession.
findings.counterevidence: V7 and the Czar/Kaiser/Mikado clause survive. The Coal-power and Gun-power terms remain in para 15.

findings.claim: The first draft cut 'He had under his eyes the whole educational staff of the Government'. The revision reduces para 16 to a sentence about Hay alone and drops the 'machinery of politics' sentence. 'These two minds' (Hay and Adams) is therefore unsupported.
findings.counterevidence: Hay and the scholar are the only individuals in focus, so the pairing is inferable.

findings.minimal_repair: Write 'to train these two minds—Hay's and his own—' and restore the 'machinery of politics' sentence.
findings.plan_relation: Para 17 compression is optional, but V6's setup function depends on it.

findings.claim: The revision removes the 'assassination as hysteria... rest-cure' sentence from the opening. It also cuts 'had singed his wings in them all' from the moth, which was the experiential cause of its instinct.
findings.counterevidence: The essential 'three political murders' irony and the north-side moth image survive.

findings.counterevidence: Hostility and isolation are still stated.

strengths: Hay's King lament is preserved whole, so 'Ca vous amuse, la vie?' lands first in Hay's voice and then flips into Adams's weary refrain in para 4.
The Seneca/Nero parable flows into the gray-headed moth on the north side of La Fayette Square, keeping the classical-to-comic deflation.
The Adams/Lodge Bostonian mirror survives intact through 'conservative Christian anarchy' and the punchline 'but he was not a Senator'.
Restoring 'nurtured in ideas of the eighteenth century' recovers the self-mocking student persona before the Jaures/Bebel paradox.
summary: The revision keeps the chapter's architecture: the 1901 griefs, King's funeral, Roosevelt as pure act, Seneca and the moth, power as poison, Lodge and the Boston double standard, forces in politics, Hay's combine and the socialist paradox, and the closing ignorance. All seven verbatim passages and the three dependencies survive. Its further cuts, mostly beyond the first draft's, remove several hinges: Hay's name before the King lament, Lodge's 'merit of interesting', the application of the double-standard maxim to Roosevelt and Lodge, and the 'mechanical assurance' concession before the final ignorance. The first draft had already left 'these two minds' without clear support. No blocker was found, but several small restorations are warranted.
